newsitem.title: USA: UAW local may strike at GM plant in Kansas.
newsitem.headline: UAW local may strike at GM plant in Kansas.

text.p: Members of a United Auto Workers (UAW) local voted to strike if a dispute with management at General Motors Corp's Fairfax, Kansas., plant cannot be resolved, a union representative said Thursday.

More than 2,000 workers, out of about 3,500 who belong the local, voted on the proposal Wednesday night, and 90.5 percent of the vote was in favor of striking if necessary, said Dan Mallett, bargaining chairman of UAW Local 31.
"At this time we're still talking. A strike is the last resort. Hopefully we can avert it," Mallett told Reuters.

Mallett said the dispute centers on the production of more vehicles at the Fairfax plant without hiring more employees. The local wants the plant to hire 150 more workers, although safety issues were also part of the dispute, Mallett said.
Janine Fruehan, a GM spokeswoman, told Reuters there were "issues between the company and the union that need to be resolved," but she declined to provide details.
Mallett said the UAW's international office would send a representative to participate in talks next week between plant managers and local union members.
The international would have to approve the local's request to strike, but Mallett said he already had the go-ahead from the international if needed.

"I've been in discussion with the international for the last three months, and before I went this far I talked with them about whether they'd give us a strike authorization. If we need it, they'll give it to us," Mallett said.

The Fairfax plant produces the Pontiac Grand Prix and the Oldsmobile Cutlass Supreme. Workers at the plant recently began building the new Oldsmobile Intrigue, which was due to reach dealers' showrooms in June.
The Kansas City Star newspaper said Thursday the Fairfax plant currently operates two shifts and produces 75 cars an hour.
